summary: Reedy Island Range Rear Light, Delaware: a 1910 cast-iron skeleton range tower at Taylor's Bridge, automated, still lit; its keepers served 1904 to 1939.

light.note: Temporary rear light first shown 16 February 1904 (DBLHKFA); the permanent tower's lamp was first lit 27 July 1910.

lens.note: The 1910 report, as LighthouseFriends quotes it, describes a fifth-order range lens. The nomination says the present light is not the original apparatus (NRHP section 7).

structures.note: 110 ft (33.5 m) above the ground per the nomination; the 1910 report gives about 125 ft total height as LighthouseFriends quotes it. 35 ft (11 m) square at the base, 10 ft (3 m) at the top; nine legs on concrete pads, replaced in January 1989.

staffing.note: Year of automation not given in these sources. The keeper roster ends in 1939.

access.note: Grounds and tower closed (LighthouseFriends). Coast Guard property. Visible alongside Taylor's Bridge Road (Route 9).

events.note: Temporary rear light first shown 16 February 1904, on a pole. Height disputed: 100-foot lantern post (DBLHKFA), 120 feet (LighthouseFriends).
Keeper's dwelling, oil house and barn begun 7 May 1906, after two rejected rounds of bids.
Lamp inside the tower lit for the first time on 27 July 1910; the temporary light was discontinued.
Fifth-order range lens per the 1910 report, supplied by the Macbeth-Evans Glass Co. of Pittsburgh (as LighthouseFriends quotes the report).
Bureau of Lighthouses absorbed into the Coast Guard; the keeper roster ends this year.
Cracked foundation pads replaced with duplicates of the originals, January 1989.
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places. The nomination carries a federal signature dated 2/22/89; the Keeper's date of action is blank in the copy read.
Fire on the evening of 6 April 2002 destroyed the keeper's dwelling and badly damaged the oil house.
Crumbling piers supporting the tower repaired around 2019.
Light made available to eligible entities under the National Historic Lighthouse Preservation Act of 2000 on 20 February 2025. None took it.
Online auction of the property opened 16 June 2026, as LighthouseFriends reports.

corrections.why: The 1896 first exhibition belongs to an earlier rear light at Port Penn Wharf (Light-House Board FY1896, entry 435). This tower's permanent lamp was first lit 27 July 1910; its temporary light was first shown 16 February 1904. The record's 1896 event (Rowlett) should be removed or moved to the Port Penn structure.

notes_for_editor: 1) Record light.first_lit 1896 (Rowlett) is the Port Penn Wharf rear light first exhibited 14 March 1896 (LHB FY1896, entry 435, p. 76 per the report index), not this tower. Proposed correction 1910 in corrections. 2) Possible duplicate record us-de-reedy-island-range-rear-2 (status 'lost', approximate position 39.50074, -75.568803 from LighthouseFriends, events 1839 first_lit, 1904 first_lit, 1910 lens_installed). It appears to be this same standing light at a second position; for the editor to merge or hide. I did not change it. 3) Position: the record (39.4066, -75.5902) matches LighthouseFriends and the NRHP area. The USLHS place record sits about 10.7 km north (39.5017, -75.5700). Roster matched with --place reedy-island-range-rear after the automatic match offered candidates. 4) Characteristic: the record says FR. DBLHKFA's copy reads 'fixed re light' (garbled), the 1989 NRHP text says 'red beacon', and Wikipedia (lead only, not cited) says 'flashing white with red sector'. Left out of facts until checked against the Light List. 5) Focal height 41 m in the record is not in any page I read; omitted. 6) Height: 110 ft above ground (NRHP) against about 125 ft total (1910 report as quoted by LighthouseFriends). Left unresolved in the story. Temporary rear light: 100-ft lantern post (DBLHKFA) against 120 ft pole (LighthouseFriends). 7) The 1910 report itself was not read: it is not in the local corpus (Lighthouse Board volumes cover 1891-1901; Commissioner 1915-1922). The 1910 lamp-lighting, lens and height come from LighthouseFriends's quotation; the 27 July 1910 date is also in DBLHKFA. 8) LHB FY1900 and FY1901 quotes have no printed page: the local copies have no page index and archive.org's in-item search returned nothing for these phrases. Cited without page; check the printed page before publication. 9) Kimmey's wife-and-stairs and 5:30 am details come from LighthouseFriends's account of a 2002 Lighthouse Digest article, which I did not read; they are attributed to LighthouseFriends. 10) Automation year unknown. The February 2025 NHLPA offer and the 16 June 2026 auction come from LighthouseFriends only; the auction listing itself was not checked. 11) Not read: HAER DE-11 (loc.gov/item/de0143, 403 to fetch_text); the USCG Historian's archived page (403). A search snippet of the USCG page gives 'Station Established: 1839' for this light, which conflicts with 1904; it could not be read, so I did not use it. 12) Robert B. Davidson: the 1921 Commissioner of Lighthouses report names a 'Robert B. Davidson, assistant keeper' at another Delaware light (OCR reads 'Listen Range'). Not linked: a shared name is not enough. 13) Egg Island and Brandywine Shoal (LighthouseFriends, Kimmey's earlier posts) have station ids us-nj-egg-island and us-nj-brandywine-shoal, but no years are given, so they are not linked as other_stations. 14) Spellings: 'A. S. Kimmey' (Smyrna Times) against 'Aaron S. Kimmey' (roster); 'Taylors Bridge' (USLHS) against 'Taylor's Bridge' (NRHP, LighthouseFriends). 15) The record's 'Port Penn Range Rear' (us-de-port-penn-range-rear, USLHS, first lit 1877, deactivated 1905) may be the same Port Penn structure as the 1896 light; not resolved. 16) The NRHP 1989 listing year is from the form's federal signature date (2/22/89) and the record; the Keeper's date of action is blank in the copy read. 17) Fact-check pass 2026-10-27: each footnoted sentence was checked against the NRHP nomination, LighthouseFriends, the USLHS roster, the DBLHKFA page, the Smyrna Times page and the Light-House Board volumes. The Port Penn entry 435 (FY1896) is confirmed on p. 76: the volume's report index lists 'Reedy Island range, rear, Delaware 76' and 'Port Penn Wharf, Delaware 76'. Changes made to the story: the Lighthouse Service roster is now attributed to the U.S. Lighthouse Society archive; the 1910 report is cited through LighthouseFriends' quotation (second-hand); the family line now follows LighthouseFriends' own sentence (the story no longer says they came with him); the 2002 Lighthouse Digest article is attributed to LighthouseFriends' reference list, not presented as read; the 1904 renaming and the name confusion are cited to LighthouseFriends; the channel sentence is footnoted; the tower height is 33.5 m; the 5.62-acre figure is noted; the auction is described as initiated, as LighthouseFriends puts it. Still unverified: the 1910 Annual Report itself (not in the local corpus), the current Light List characteristic, the year of automation, the auction listing, and the printed pages of the FY1900 and FY1901 Light-House Board entries.
